name: Roland Fantom-G6/G7/G8
description: Roland Fantom-G6, Fantom-G7 and Fantom-G8 workstations (one sound engine, one address map): the setup and system blocks, the temporary Studio Set (common, insert MFX, chorus, reverb, mastering, input FX, and every internal, ARX-expansion and external part) and the temporary Live Set likewise, both modes' arpeggio and chord memory, and Studio Mode Part 1's temporary patch, sample set and rhythm set, from the MIDI Implementation.

sources.title: Roland Fantom-G6/G7/G8 MIDI Implementation
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from Fantom-G_MI.pdf (sha256 7e87d1aefda01c1a753f4352dc427f63c082d5cf52e99485c9d30f53f6b64c87). Model ID 00 00 27, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.
One profile for the Fantom-G6, G7 and G8: the Identity Reply (p9) is the same family 27 02 / 00 00 for all three, and only the first software-revision byte says which (00 G6, 01 G7, 02 G8).
The manual prints no version or date on its first page. Its MIDI Implementation Charts (p46, p47) say Version 1.00, Feb. 1, 2008; every page's FrameMaker running head is stamped 8 May 2008.

Model id 00 00 27, as the address map's heading (p14), the DT1 and RQ1 byte tables (p6, p10) and the worked example's byte diagram (p45) give it. The prose on p6 ("The model ID of the exclusive messages used by this instrument is 00H 27H"), the RQ1/DT1 status lines on p6 and p10 ("41H, dev, 00H, 27H, 12H") and the example's closing line on p45 ("F0 41 10 00 27 12 10 00 06 00 02 68 F7") print two bytes, 00 27, which is the Fantom-X's pattern (00 6B). The checksum (68) is the same either way, since it covers only the address and the data.

The worked example on p45 is introduced as "CHORUS TYPE of LIVE SET" and then calls the address that of "CHORUS TYPE of PERFORMANCE COMMON", an older manual's words; the address, 10 00 06 00, is the Live Set's.

Studio Mode Part 1's rhythm set: keys 35 (B1) to 59 (B3) are laid out, 25 of the 88, to keep the profile near 12,000 parameters; keys 21-34 and 60-108 are the same two blocks again, two apart (00 02 00), from 19 10 10 00 and 19 12 10 00.

Not laid out: the temporary sounds of Studio Mode Parts 2-16 (19 20 00 00 … 1C 60 00 00) and of Live Mode Parts 1-8 (11 00 00 00 … 12 60 00 00), each a patch (+00 00 00), sample set (+08 00 00) and rhythm set (+10 00 00) like Part 1's.
Exp n Part m is part m of the ARX expansion board in slot n (its own sixteen parts), not internal Part m; the Exp n Common blocks are that board's level, pan, sends and output in the set.

The Live Set has eight internal parts (Live Set Part, 00 20 00 - 00 27 00, p14) but sixteen MIDI channels, sixteen parts per ARX slot and sixteen external parts; its insert MFX, mastering and input FX are the System's (02 00 02 00, 02 00 0E 00, 02 00 0F 00).
Studio Set Controller 00 25 is printed "Arpeggio Swich" (p27; the Live Set Controller prints "Arpeggio Switch"), so its id is studioSet.controller.arpeggioSwich.
Rhythm Common Reverb's Reverb Output Assign is printed (0 - 3) with the labels A, B (p38); the other four Reverb Output Assign rows print (0 - 1). It is kept as the manual prints it, a number 0-3.
p14 says "<*>" marked rows are ignored "when the Fantom-G6/X7/X8 received them": X7 and X8 are the Fantom-X's model names. The "<*>" (reserve) rows are not laid out.

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: what the front panel transmits (Control Change, pp7-8) is not in the address map
coverage.parts: the Studio Set's 16 parts and the Live Set's 8, with every ARX-expansion part (Exp1/Exp2, 16 each) and external part (16) of both; the temporary sound of Studio Mode Part 1 only, in all three kinds (patch, sample set, rhythm set). Studio Mode Parts 2-16 are at 19 00 00 00 + (n-1) x 00 20 00 00 (19 20 00 00, 19 40 00 00, … 1C 60 00 00) and Live Mode Parts 1-8 at 11 00 00 00 + (n-1) x 00 20 00 00 (11 00 00 00 … 12 60 00 00), each with a patch at +00 00 00, a sample set at +08 00 00 and a rhythm set at +10 00 00; they are not laid out
coverage.rhythmKeys: Studio Mode Part 1's rhythm set for keys 35-59 only (Rhythm Tone and Rhythm Tone 2). The map has keys 21-108: Rhythm Tone (Key # k) is at 19 10 10 00 + (k-21) x 00 02 00 and Rhythm Tone 2 (Key # k) at 19 12 10 00 + (k-21) x 00 02 00, so keys 21-34 are at 19 10 10 00-19 10 2A 00 / 19 12 10 00-19 12 2A 00 and keys 60-108 at 19 10 5E 00-19 11 3E 00 / 19 12 5E 00-19 13 3E 00; all eighty-eight would be 12,848 parameters
coverage.toneTypes: a part plays a patch, a sample set or a rhythm set; the blocks of all three are laid out at their addresses, and the manual says (p6) that a request it cannot answer gets no reply, so none of them is read at startup (noPull); each is read when asked for
coverage.reserveOnlyBlocks: Patch Controller (+00 60 00) and Rhythm Controller (+03 60 00) are printed entirely as "(reserve)" and are not laid out
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: type-dependent: MFX, chorus, reverb and input-effect parameters are Roland's 4-nibble container (12768-52768, shown -20000..+20000); what each slot does depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list
coverage.arx: the ARX expansion boards' own sound parameters are not in this manual (p1 refers to the ARX owner's manuals); only the Exp1/Exp2 common and part mixing blocks of each set are laid out
coverage.presets: Studio Set banks (MSB 85) and Live Set banks (MSB 84) as printed on p1; the Preset Live Set rows after LSB 064 are elided with ":" and are not listed. They are recalled on the profile's channel, which must be the Studio Set Control Channel (System Common 00 0B) for a studio set and the Live Set Control Channel (00 0A) for a live set
